claims.text: A properly calibrated CALPHAD approach can accurately predict melting temperatures across the high-entropy-alloy family.
A properly calibrated CALPHAD approach can accurately predict enthalpies and entropies of fusion across the high-entropy-alloy family.
A properly calibrated CALPHAD approach can accurately predict volume changes at melting across the high-entropy-alloy family.
A properly calibrated CALPHAD approach can accurately predict associated liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across the high-entropy-alloy family.
CALPHAD should be calibrated by fitting to multi-property experimental datasets from DSC, dilatometry, and high-temperature X-ray diffraction that are specific to high-entropy alloys.
CALPHAD-derived thermodynamic-potential surfaces and equilibrium phase boundaries mediate the relationship between composition, phase stability, and fusion properties.
CALPHAD uses thermodynamically consistent databases and interaction parameters.

Fine-tuning CALPHAD interaction parameters with multi-property experimental data makes predicted phase equilibria accurately reflect the underlying physics and interatomic interactions of complex high-entropy systems.

Fine-tuning CALPHAD interaction parameters with multi-property experimental data makes predicted melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, and melting-related volume change accurately reflect the underlying physics of high-entropy systems.
Calibrated CALPHAD melting-temperature predictions will agree with experiments to approximately ±10%.
Calibrated CALPHAD predictions of fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, and volume change at melting will achieve approximately similar quantitative agreement.
The calibrated model will significantly reduce the need for extensive experimental probing.
Uncalibrated CALPHAD predictions typically have larger errors and uncertainties for fusion properties in high-entropy alloys.
The approach will be most effective for compositions and interaction regimes already well represented in thermodynamic databases.
Predictive accuracy may decline for extreme compositions or novel interactions outside the calibrated range.
The extrapolative performance of the method beyond its calibrated regime is not established.
